summary: Aletheai is a behavioural decision-intelligence company. Its engine reads behavioural signals from the systems a business already runs, ranks who or what deserves attention by the evidence, attaches a plain-English reason and next action to every item, and declines to rank where the evidence is insufficient.
status: First market: UK estate agency, launching through the Alto (Zoopla Group) marketplace; first cohort recruiting.
patents_line: Six patent applications filed, 2025–2026 (UK and international). Two are summarised below; the others are unpublished.

patents.label: Patent application · international (PCT), priority September 2025
patents.title: Behavioural decision intelligence
patents.text: An engine that ranks who or what deserves attention by the evidence rather than a score over everything, attaches a plain-English reason and next action to every item, and refuses to rank where the evidence is insufficient, with the refusal recorded. Its behavioural archetypes live in a fixed, versioned library that changes only at signed releases, never silently in production.

patents.label: Patent application · UK, September 2026
patents.title: Action gating for AI agents
patents.text: Every act an AI agent takes passes through a gate the agent cannot reach, is registered before it happens, and must be justified by evidence the agent did not write. The gate uses no model: it is deterministic and replayable, so oversight does not depend on reading the agent's reasoning. Governance of machine conduct, not machine thought.

questions: When should a machine decline to answer?
Ranking only where the evidence supports it, and recording the refusal, so a person can see where the system could not see.
How do you govern what an AI agent does without reading its mind?
Gate the action, not the reasoning: evidence the agent did not write, checked by a gate it cannot reach.
What does it take for a decision to be defensible afterwards?
A record a person can open: what was known, what was inferred, and why this item came first.
partners: Feasibility study on real human-behaviour datasets, including how to treat missing data before trusting a model on it.
